ops.title: Styleguide gate blind to non-Edit/Write file changes — forensics for the gate fix
ops.body:
**Root cause (CONFIRMED, session be21e6e5, 2026-07-16/17).** The `.claude/hooks/style.py` `gate()` never fired during the session that authored the rm-guard (commit 8e32bb48) because its `when=` reads `evt.ctx.t.tool_calls.named("Edit|Write").files()` — a *tool-identity* filter. The implementation was written by codex CLI subprocesses launched via the Bash tool and staged with plain `git add`: **zero** Edit/Write tool_use blocks on `captain_hook/**/*.py` exist in the whole transcript, so `when()` evaluated cleanly to False on all 8 Stop dispatches. The python pack's `styleguide()` rules (PostToolUse gated by `Tool("Edit|Write")`) share the same blindness.

**Refuted alternatives (evidence-checked):** hookd staleness (daemon fingerprints `.claude/hooks` per request; transcript cache is mtime-exact via `daemon/transcache.py`), swallowed `when()` exception (`dispatch.py:34-35` logs handler exceptions bound to hook name; session log has zero style entries), gate throttling (`primitives/nudge.py:112` — block=True resolves to `max_fires=None`, per-turn re-arm; no fire ever consumed), `is_test` misclassification (`cc_transcript/query.py:112,121-123` — only `test_*`/`conftest`/`tests/` match), gate file added late (exists since 2026-06-05, last touched 2026-06-22).

**Two distinct gaps:**
1. **Active:** files modified by any Bash-spawned subprocess (codex exec, `ccx code edit`, sed, heredocs) produce only an opaque Bash tool_use — invisible to tool-name filters. This is the standard implementation lane in this fleet (codex/sol routing), so the gate was structurally blind to the very workflow that writes most code here.
2. **Latent:** `Session.tool_calls` (`cc_transcript/query.py:299-301`) is built from the session's own turns and never recurses into `Session.subagents` — Task/Agent-authored edits are equally invisible.

**Evaluated fix options (for whoever picks this up):**
1. Key `when=` off filesystem truth: `evt.ctx.changed_paths` (`captain_hook/context.py:187-191`, cached frozenset from `git diff --name-only HEAD --no-renames`) or `evt.ctx.diff()` (`context.py:138-175`). Tool-agnostic; goes blind after a mid-session commit, and in a shared working copy fires on OTHER sessions' dirty files (real here — concurrent sessions routinely hold WIP).
2. Intersection: changed_paths ∩ session-attributable paths (Edit/Write files ∪ paths named in this session's Bash command strings). Precise across concurrent sessions; misses pathless flows (`git add -A`).
3. Recurse subagents in the tool_calls view — closes gap 2 only.
4. PostToolUse-on-Bash working-tree diffing — precise attribution, one git status per Bash call.

Full evidence chain lives in session transcript be21e6e5-dd14-4bbc-8237-121c23aaf3d8 (jq counts, fire-log queries, git history).
